decision.explanation: Since a₁=2a₂, a₂ is redundant. The determinant of the matrix with columns a₁ and a₃ is 4(7)-6(-2)=40≠0, so these vectors are linearly independent and form a basis of the span.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ -2 & -1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}.
$$

content.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ -2 & -1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}.
$$

after.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ ${a}_{3},$ and ${a}_{4}$ are given below. Determine whether $B={{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3},$ where ${a}_{4}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ -16\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+{x}_{3}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ -16\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-3 \\ -{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=3 \\ 6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}+7{x}_{3}=-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & -6 & 7 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & -6 & 7 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=2,$ meaning that

$$
(-5)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+0\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ -16\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=(-5)+0+2=-3.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]

after.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+{x}_{3}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-4 \\ -9{x}_{1}-8{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -4 \\ -9 & 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -15 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-15,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=17,$ meaning that

$$
(-15)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+0\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+17\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=(-15)+0+17=2.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -16\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 6 \\ 8 & 3 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ 8 & 3 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 11 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}.
$$

content.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -16\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 6 \\ 8 & 3 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ 8 & 3 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 11 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}.
$$
